problem:
Solve the following system of equations:
    

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+z=\frac{1}{2} \\  & y+z=1 \\  & z=2\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:
    

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=4 \\  & {x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=2 \\  & {x}_{3}=-2\end{aligned}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
The third equation states that ${x}_{3}=-2.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}+(-2)=2\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=2+2=4.
$$

Now, we substitute ${x}_{2}=4$ and ${x}_{3}=-2$ into the first equation to get

$$
{x}_{1}-4-(-2)=4\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=4+4-2=6.
$$

Therefore, the solution is ${x}_{1}=6$, ${x}_{2}=4$, and ${x}_{3}=-2.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨6,4,-2⟩.$
